info.title: The Bazaar API
info.description: The Bazaar, a multi-vendor market: catalogue, cart, checkout, orders, store space rental, rider hiring and dispatch, and live updates over /ws/live. Everyone signs in on one page with email and password through Supabase Auth; GET /me says which role the account has and where to send it. Authenticate with a Supabase access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Money is integer cents with a currency code. Errors look like `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`.

get.description:
Stall plans without prices. Rent and commission are set by the admin
(PATCH /admin/plans/{id}) and shown to a vendor in their own back office
once they're on a plan.

get.description:
Who is signed in and where they belong. After the one login page, the
frontend sends people to `home`: shoppers to the storefront, vendors to
their back office, riders to their jobs, admins to the console, and
riders who aren't hired yet to the hiring page.

schema.title: Response List Addresses Api V1 Me Addresses Get

post.description: Move a cart line to the wishlist.

Turns the cart (or the `items` sent) into an order.

Only variant ids and quantities are read from the client. Prices, volume
tiers, coupons, shipping and tax are all worked out by place_order() in
the database while the stock rows are locked.

put.description:
Move the drop-off pin, for example to the gate the rider should come
to. Works until the parcel is delivered. A rider already on the way sees
the new pin straight away.

post.description:
Switch plan. The new rent applies from the next billing date; the
commission rate applies to orders placed from now on.

delete.description:
Products that have been ordered are archived, not deleted, so order
history keeps its links.

post.description: Add a picture to the end of the product's gallery (12 at most).

put.description: Swap one picture for a new file, keeping its place in the gallery.

Send every image id of the product in the order to show them. The
first one is the cover picture.

Add the product's video, or replace the one it has. Each product has
one video next to its photos.

post.description:
Older direct-to-Storage upload. The bucket only takes images up to
5 MB, but the file isn't cleaned. Use POST /seller/products/{id}/images.

schema.title: Response My Placements Api V1 Seller Placements Get

patch.description:
Update stock for up to 200 variants at once. All or nothing: if one
line is wrong, nothing changes. Every change is kept in the history.

get.description:
Who changed stock by hand, when, and why. Sales aren't listed here;
they're on the orders.

post.description:
Stores no longer confirm payments. Shoppers pay The Bazaar's till,
and the rider at the door (or an admin) confirms it by the transaction
code. Kept so old clients get a clear answer: always 403.

schema.title: Response Available Riders Api V1 Seller Riders Available Get

get.description:
Riders on the store's jobs, riders who delivered for it lately, and
free riders close to the shop, closest first within each group. Each row
carries what the expandable panel shows: contact, vehicle, live position
and recent jobs for this store.

schema.title: Response Store Riders Api V1 Seller Riders Get

post.description:
Send a rider for the order. Leave rider_id out to send the closest
free rider to the shop (409 "no_riders" if nobody is on shift nearby;
the order then stays on automatic dispatch and goes to the first rider
who frees up). Orders are normally dispatched automatically as soon as
they're ready, so this is for re-sending after a failed attempt, or for
choosing a particular rider.

Pull a job back from a rider who hasn't collected it yet. The order
comes off automatic dispatch, so it waits for the store to choose the
next rider (or to dispatch again with no rider to go back to automatic).

get.description:
Read-only sheets, built from the books themselves: ledger (every
movement of the store's balance), sales (items sold and paid), payments
(each order, its transaction codes and the store's share), inventory
(stock and units sold), entries (vendor sheet rows an admin confirmed) and
payouts. Filter by date with from and to. format=csv downloads the lot. Your store only.

patch.description: Editing a rejected entry sends it back to the admin as pending.

schema.title: Response Entry History Api V1 Seller Sheet Entries  Entry Id  History Get

post.description:
The hiring form. Open to riders who signed up through the rider link
and to existing shoppers. The application lands on the admins' hiring
page, and the account gets rider access only once an admin hires it.

get.description:
The rider's profile, or the state of their application while they
wait: status is "applicant" until an admin decides, then "active" or
"rejected". 404 means they haven't applied yet.

post.description: Send every 10 to 15 seconds while on shift.

patch.description:
accept or decline an offer, then picked_up at the shop, and delivered
at the door with the shopper's 6 digit handover code once the payment
is confirmed (POST .../payment). failed needs a note.

get.description:
Jobs waiting for a rider near you, and offers made to you, oldest
order first (offers on top). While you're on a run, a job you can't add
to it comes back with batchable false and the reason, so the app can
grey it out. Needs you on shift with a recent location.

post.description:
Take a job from the board. It goes straight to accepted and joins your
run. If it was offered to you, this accepts the offer.

Not interested. The job leaves your board and won't be offered to you
again. An offer you skip is declined and passes to the next rider.

get.description:
The jobs on your current run in the order they were placed, and the
way to go: shops you still have to collect from, then drop-offs, oldest
order first. Stops stay on the run (delivered ones too) until you start
the next one.

post.description:
You're at the drop-off. Admins get a payment check ping, and the
shopper is told to pay the till now, quoting their order number.

get.description:
What's still owed at this door, and the payments that match q: a
transaction code (exact) or the payer's name (3 or more letters, up to 3
recent unused payments, codes masked). A used code shows used: true and
nothing else about it.

post.description:
Use a payment for this order: by its transaction code, or by the
receipt_id a name search returned. The payment is spent for good; using
it again anywhere fails with 409 code_used. Partial payments add up.

patch.description:
Fees take effect for orders placed from now on; orders already placed
keep what they were charged.

get.description:
What the marketplace itself earns. Everything is read off the store
ledgers: a debit on a store is income for the platform.

post.description: For transfers made to The Bazaar's own account.

get.description:
Everything for the expandable row: contact, last position and
heading, and the latest 20 jobs.
The hiring queue: riders who filled in the form and are waiting.

post.description:
Hire the rider. Their account switches to the rider role and they can
sign in to the rider app.
Turn the application down. The note is shown to the applicant.

get.description:
Everything for the admin's live map. Subscribe to the websocket with
scope "admin" for updates.

post.description:
Mark all of a rider's unpaid earnings as paid out (after you've paid
them outside the app).
Runs the same jobs the worker runs on a timer.

Paste the till's or bank's messages, as many as you like. Each one is
read for the transaction code, amount, payer and time. With commit false
nothing is stored, so you can check the reading first. A code already in
the bank is never stored twice.

get.description:
What each store is owed. Takings become owed once they've been held
for the payout interval; rent, commission, fees and delivery charges
are already taken off. Books balance when every delivered order has a
confirmed payment and the store has no sheet entries waiting.

schema.title: Response Settlements Api V1 Admin Settlements Get

post.description: Record that you've paid a store. Defaults to everything owed.

get.description:
Read-only sheets, built from the books themselves: ledger (every
movement of the store's balance), sales (items sold and paid), payments
(each order, its transaction codes and the store's share), inventory
(stock and units sold), entries (vendor sheet rows an admin confirmed) and
payouts. Filter by date with from and to. format=csv downloads the lot. Every store, or one with store_id.

post.description:
For an SMS forwarding app on the phone that receives the till's
messages: POST {"text": "..."} here. The token is PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_TOKEN.

get.description:
Maintenance state, the fees the cart should show, and the admin
contact the rent-a-stall page shows instead of prices.

PublicPlan.title: PublicPlan
PublicPlan.description:
A stall plan as the public sees it: what it includes, not what it
costs. Prices are agreed with the admin; GET /status has the contact.

RiderRules.title: RiderRules
RiderRules.description: The admin's rules for riders, so the app can explain what's locked.

owed_cents.title: Owed Cents
owed_cents.description: Takings past the holding period, after rent, commission and delivery.

held_cents.title: Held Cents
held_cents.description: Takings still inside the payout interval.

net_cents.title: Net Cents
net_cents.description: What a settlement now would pay: owed_cents if positive.

StockChange.title: StockChange
StockChange.description:
Set `stock` to a count, or move it by `adjust_by` (a delivery in, a
damaged item out). `adjust_by` is safer while orders are coming in,
because it doesn't overwrite a sale that happened a second ago.

StoreRider.title: StoreRider
StoreRider.description:
A rider as a store sees them. `relation` says why they're listed:
on_job (carrying or about to carry one of the store's orders), recent
(delivered for the store in the last 30 days) or nearby (on shift, free
and close to the shop). Phone numbers are shown for riders who work the
store's orders, never for strangers nearby, and the exact position only
while the rider is out on one of the store's jobs. completed_deliveries
counts deliveries for this store in the last 30 days.
